> **What this case shows** — the ecosystem's entropies (permutation, sample, spectral) are all
> *Shannon*. The **Renyi entropy** is a one-parameter *family* that contains Shannon as a special
> case: at order **α = 1** it *is* Shannon, at **α = 2** the collision entropy, at **α → ∞** the
> min-entropy, and it is non-increasing in α. This case introduces a **newly-authored op**,
> `renyiEntropy`. On a real eyes-closed EEG channel it reproduces `NeuroKit2.entropy_renyi`
> **bit-for-bit** (max |diff| ~**4e-16**) across **α = {0.5, 1, 2, 3}** — the α = 1 value exactly
> recovers the **Shannon entropy** (2.325 nats), and the family is monotonically decreasing in α.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — for the generalized entropy: `renyiEntropy(x, alpha, bins)` → the order-α entropy of the
signal's amplitude distribution (nats).
**Way of thinking** — one number (Shannon) is a slice of a curve. Sweeping α gives the *Renyi
spectrum*: α < 1 weights rare amplitudes, α > 1 weights frequent ones — a richer fingerprint of the
distribution than any single entropy.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioEEG::renyiEntropy()`; `alpha = 1` for Shannon, `alpha = 2` for collision.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed POz EEG, `renyiEntropy` reproduces `NeuroKit2.entropy_renyi` bit-for-bit (max
|diff| ~4e-16) across α = {0.5, 1, 2, 3}; α = 1 recovers Shannon (2.325 nats), and H_α is
non-increasing in α.

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and its fidelity: the ecosystem had only Shannon entropies — can we author
the generalized Renyi family and reproduce the reference across α, with the right mathematical
structure (Shannon at α = 1, monotonic)?** The goal is to introduce `renyiEntropy`, certify it
bit-for-bit across the family, and verify its defining properties.

## Challenge & approach

Renyi entropy is H_α = 1/(1−α)·ln(Σ p_i^α), where p is the signal's amplitude histogram. We implement
that closed form (with the Shannon limit at α = 1) and check it against `NeuroKit2.entropy_renyi` on
the identical histogram, across a range of α.

```
EEG POz (eegmmidb) → renyiEntropy(alpha, bins = 16) → H_α
                    vs NeuroKit2.entropy_renyi (same histogram) → bit-exact (~4e-16) for every α
                    α=1 → Shannon (2.325); α=2 → collision (2.167); non-increasing in α
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02
(eyes-closed)**, channel **POz**, 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked vector the
[SVD-entropy](../svd-entropy-eegmmidb/index.qmd) and [Petrosian](../petrosian-fd-eegmmidb/index.qmd)
cases use. Details in [`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

Right: the POz amplitude histogram (16 bins) — the distribution whose generalized entropy is computed.](artifacts/figure.png)

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **Renyi entropy, α = 1 (Shannon)** | **2.325 nats** |
| **Renyi entropy, α = 2 (collision)** | **2.167 nats** |
| op vs `NeuroKit2.entropy_renyi` (max \|diff\| over the family) | **4e-16** (bit-exact) |
| bins | **16** |
| non-increasing in α | **yes** |

The newly-authored op equals NeuroKit2 at every α, recovers Shannon at α = 1, and is monotonic —
the family's defining structure. Values trace to
[`artifacts/renyi_summary.csv`](artifacts/renyi_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`renyiEntropy` fills a real gap — the ecosystem had only Shannon entropies, not the generalized family
— and it is exact: bit-for-bit against NeuroKit2 across α, with Shannon recovered at α = 1 and the
correct monotonic structure. The transferable takeaway: **Shannon entropy is one point on the Renyi
curve; sweep α to get the whole spectrum, and use α = 2 (collision) when you want a
concentration-sensitive alternative to Shannon.**

## Open questions

- The Renyi spectrum's α-dependence characterizes a distribution's tail structure; computing it across
  EEG states (eyes-open vs eyes-closed) or channels — and its curvature — would turn the single-α
  value into a multifractal-like descriptor. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Renyi entropy (generalized, order α) | `renyiEntropy()` | PhysioEEG |
| SVD entropy / Petrosian FD | `svdEntropy()`, `petrosianFD()` | PhysioEEG |
| multi-measure complexity (Shannon-based) | `eegComplexity()` | PhysioEEG |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **alpha** — `1` is Shannon, `2` the collision entropy (concentration-sensitive), larger α weights
  the most frequent amplitudes (→ min-entropy); sweep α for the Renyi spectrum.
- **bins** — the amplitude-histogram resolution (here 16); more bins resolve finer structure but need
  more data, and the absolute value is bin-dependent.
- **units** — nats (natural log), as in `NeuroKit2.entropy_renyi`.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioEEG)

renyiEntropy(x, alpha = 2)   # collision entropy (nats)
renyiEntropy(x, alpha = 1)   # = Shannon entropy

# reproduces NeuroKit2.entropy_renyi bit-for-bit across alpha (max |diff| ~4e-16).
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/renyi_summary.csv`](artifacts/renyi_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the
collision and Shannon entropies, the bit-exact NeuroKit2 match over the α family, the monotonicity and
the α = 1 = Shannon relationship, and the honestly-noted scope (newly-authored op; histogram-dependent;
structure not absolute value).
